# A click inside the portal's scroll container never becomes actionable

## Context

Splitting out the one open item from #17877, whose own prescription shipped in PR #17859 and which is now closed. The residual is **not** a link-rewrite question and never was — it is a harness-capability question that blocks a whole tier of portal coverage.

Measured by @neo-opus-ada on 2026-08-30 ([comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17877#issuecomment-5465997906)) while chasing a click-through arm:

```
goto  #/learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts   → h1 "Dock Layouts: One Application, Many Windows"
location.hash = '#/learn/benefits/body/Speed'       → h1 "Extreme Speed"
```

Hash navigation works — router, exact-id `store.get`, record fetch and re-render all run in about four seconds. **What fails is `locator.click`**, which exceeds the 90 000 ms ceiling at `test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs:95`. Playwright never satisfies its visible / stable / receives-events checks for content inside the portal's scroll container.

## The Problem

The decisive datum is the **control**: clicking the sidebar tree item fails identically. That element is the app's own navigation and owes nothing to the link rewrite. A red assertion whose control is also red measures the harness, not the subject — so the click arm was written and correctly reverted rather than shipped as a false "routing is broken" signal.

That leaves a documented hole, in prose, at `test/playwright/e2e/portal/LearnLinkRoutingNL.spec.mjs:51-61`:

> Not covered here, and deliberately not asserted: that CLICKING one of these links arrives at the destination.

The cost is not one missing assertion. **No portal e2e arm can currently assert that clicking anything arrives**, so every future arm in this tier inherits the same gap and the same temptation to paper over it with `force: true`. Ada declined to file it at the time because the seats that would pick it up were rate-limited — that constraint has expired, and the measurement should not die with the ticket that hosted it.

## The Architectural Reality

- Content renders into `.neo-app-content-component` (`src/app/content/Component.mjs`), inside the portal's scrolling content region.
- Neo applies DOM deltas from the app worker on the main thread. An element that is repeatedly re-written by delta application can fail Playwright's **stable** check (two consecutive animation frames at the same box) without ever being invisible — a distinct failure from occlusion.
- The three actionability checks fail for different reasons and are **not** distinguishable from the timeout message alone. Which one fails is the whole finding, and nothing has measured it yet.
- Sibling precedent for a shared harness helper is `test/playwright/util/` — `learnLinkNavigability.mjs`, `DeltaCapture.mjs`, `flickerCensus.mjs`. A new helper belongs there, not beside a single spec.

## The Fix

1. Determine **which** actionability check fails, against the sidebar-tree control rather than the rewritten anchor — the control is the honest subject, because it isolates the harness from the feature.
2. Fix the cause at the layer that owns it: a scroll/stability helper in `test/playwright/util/`, or an e2e config/`use` adjustment if the cause is global.
3. Only then add the click arm to `LearnLinkRoutingNL.spec.mjs` and delete the prose gap at `:51-61`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The failing actionability check is named — visible, stable, or receives-events — with the measurement that identifies it, not inferred from the timeout text
- [ ] The **control passes first**: clicking the portal sidebar tree item navigates, in the e2e harness, before any assertion is added about an in-content link
- [ ] A click on a rewritten in-content link arrives at its destination (destination `h1` asserted), and the deliberate-gap comment at `test/playwright/e2e/portal/LearnLinkRoutingNL.spec.mjs:51-61` is deleted in the same PR
- [ ] The arm is proven able to fail: deleting the `rewriteLinks` invocation or the portal's `contentRoute` reddens it — the mutation the sibling href arms already survive
- [ ] No `force: true`, no `dispatchEvent`, and no raised timeout: the arm exercises what a reader's pointer does
- [ ] If the cause is general to the tier, the remedy is a shared helper under `test/playwright/util/` rather than a per-spec workaround

## Out of Scope

- The link rewrite itself — `rewriteLinks`, `contentRoute_`, and the portal declaration shipped in PR #17859 and are verified by the corpus, predicate-parity and href arms.
- Whether routing works. It does; that was measured and is not in question here.
- Guide links into repository **source** files. Reported separately by the corpus sweep, and a live question about whether guides should link to source at all.

## Avoided Traps

| Tempting | Why it is wrong here |
|---|---|
| `click({force: true})` | Skips the actionability checks entirely. The arm goes green while the reader's click is still broken — it asserts the absence of the measurement, not the presence of the behavior. |
| Raising the e2e timeout | 90 s was already exceeded. This is not slowness, and a higher ceiling only makes the red slower to arrive. |
| `dispatchEvent` / synthetic event | A discrete synthetic event is not a pointer gesture; it bypasses exactly the hit-testing this ticket exists to prove. |
| Shipping the click arm with a red control | Already tried and correctly reverted. It reads as "routing is broken" on evidence that says nothing of the kind. |
